title: Chrysler Building
blurb: William Van Alen's Art Deco skyscraper at 405 Lexington Avenue, completed 27 May 1930, in simplified schematic form: a secret 185 ft stainless steel spire, seven radiating terraced arches, and a shaft dressed in automobile ornament.

systems.name: Shaft and facade
systems.description: The setback tower mass in four stages, with horizontal window bands in white and dark-gray brick emphasizing the window rows.

systems.name: Crown
systems.description: The seven radiating terraced arches with stylized sunburst panels in Nirosta stainless steel, rising from the 61st floor to the 925 ft roof.

systems.name: Spire
systems.description: The secret 185 ft Nirosta stainless steel spire, assembled inside the crown and raised through the roof in 90 minutes on 23 October 1929.

systems.name: Automobile ornament
systems.description: Stainless steel ornament drawn from Chrysler automobiles: eagle gargoyles, radiator caps, hubcaps and wheel motifs, plus the street entrance portals.

systems.name: Lobby
systems.description: The three story lobby interior with Red Moroccan marble, onyx, and the Edward Trumbull ceiling murals.

systems.name: Structure and core
systems.description: The steel frame, the central core, the 32 elevators, and floor plates, revealed when the model is exploded.

systems.name: Lighting
systems.description: Floodlighting for the stainless steel crown and the spire aviation beacon.

explanations.base mass, floors 1 to 16: The base of the tower, floors 1 to 16, the widest of the setback stages. The setback above the 16th floor is sourced; the exact footprint is schematic.
explanations.h-plan corner wings: The corner wings of the H-plan base, standing slightly proud of the main walls. The H-shaped plan is sourced; exact wing dimensions are schematic.
explanations.mid stage mass, floors 17 to 29: The merged second and third setback stages, floors 17 to 29. The setbacks below the 23rd and 30th floors are sourced; exact footprints are schematic.
explanations.upper shaft mass, floors 30 to 61: The main shaft, floors 30 to 61, carrying the eagle gargoyles at its corners and the crown above. The exact footprint is schematic.
explanations.window bands: Merged horizontal window bands across the shaft, part of the white and dark-gray brickwork that emphasizes the horizontal window rows. Band positions are schematic.
explanations.dark-gray spandrel courses: Dark-gray brick spandrel courses at the setback levels, emphasizing the horizontal window rows. Positions are schematic.
explanations.crown arch bands: The seven radiating terraced arches of the crown, merged into one part, clad in Nirosta stainless steel. Arch profiles are schematic.
explanations.crown sunburst fins: The stylized sunburst fins of the crown, merged into one part: radiating stainless steel fins that give the crown its sunrise motif. Arrangement is schematic.
explanations.spire base collar: The collar where the spire passes through the roof at 925 ft (282 m). The spire was secretly assembled inside the crown and raised through the roof in 90 minutes on 23 October 1929. Form shown schematically.
explanations.lower spire: The lower half of the secret 185 ft (56 m), 27 ton Nirosta stainless steel spire. Segment divisions are schematic.
explanations.upper spire: The upper half of the secret spire, tapering to the needle tip. Segment divisions are schematic.
explanations.needle tip: The needle tip of the spire at 1,046 ft (319 m), which made the Chrysler Building the tallest building in the world from 27 May 1930 to 1 May 1931. Exact tip form is schematic.
explanations.eagle gargoyles: The eight stylized American eagle-head gargoyles on the 61st floor corners, merged into one part. Exact forms and placement are schematic.
explanations.radiator cap replicas: The four 1929 Chrysler radiator-cap replicas on the 31st floor corners, merged into one part. Exact forms are schematic.
explanations.hubcap frieze: A frieze band of hubcap motifs ringing the 31st floor, drawn from Chrysler automobile design. Exact motif arrangement is schematic.
explanations.car wheel bands: Ornamental bands of car-wheel motifs on the shaft, merged into one part. Exact motifs are schematic.
explanations.entrance portals: The three street entrance portals on Lexington Avenue, 42nd and 43rd Streets, merged into one part. Portal designs are schematic.
explanations.lobby shell: The shell of the three story lobby interior: floor, walls and ceiling slab. Layout is schematic.
explanations.lobby marble and onyx: The Red Moroccan marble wall panels and the onyx elevator surround of the lobby, merged into one part. The lobby combines Red Moroccan marble with onyx, blue marble and steel; layout is schematic.
explanations.mural ceiling: The lobby ceiling with murals by Edward Trumbull, refurbished in 1978. Mural content is shown schematically as gold panels.
explanations.elevator doors: The four elevator doors of the lobby bank, merged into one part, from the 32 elevators in the building. Door designs are schematic.
explanations.steel column grid: The steel frame column grids through the tower, merged into one part. Shown schematically and revealed when the model is exploded.
explanations.central core shaft: The central core carrying elevators, stairs and services the full height of the building. Interior layout is schematic.
explanations.elevator banks: The 32 elevators of the building, merged into one bank part. Arrangement is schematic.
explanations.floor plates: Floor plates bracing the steel frame, including the historic Cloud Club levels on the upper floors, a private club of the late 1920s to the 1970s. Exact floors shown are schematic.
explanations.setback cornices: Cornice bands at the 16th, 23rd and 30th floor setbacks, merged into one part. The setbacks are sourced; cornice profiles are schematic.
explanations.setback terraces: Open terrace decks at the setback levels, merged into one part. Shown schematically.
explanations.roof platform and parapet: The roof platform at 925 ft (282 m) with its parapet, where the spire emerges from the crown. Shown schematically.
explanations.crown floodlights: Floodlights washing the stainless steel crown at night, merged into one part. Fixture count and placement are schematic.
explanations.spire beacon: The aviation warning beacon at the spire tip. Shown schematically.
